title: CBC, ‘Hockey Night in Canada’ will no longer carry NHL games as Sportsnet agreement ends
content:
“Hockey Night in Canada,” a decades-long Canadian institution owned by the country’s public broadcaster, appears to be finished in its iconic form.

In a joint statement with Rogers Sportsnet on Tuesday morning, CBC announced that it will no longer carry NHL games as part of a new “sports programming strategy,” which coincides with the end of Sportsnet and CBC’s 12-year sublicensing agreement. That partnership originated when Sportsnet acquired the league’s national television rights for $5.2 billion Canadian in 2013.

The two sides failed to strike a new sublicensing deal for Sportsnet to continue airing the CBC’s signature program, “Hockey Night in Canada,” which typically showed games on Saturday nights. The CBC still owns the rights to “Hockey Night in Canada” and plans to retain them.

“It’s fair to say CBC will no longer be carrying NHL hockey, however, we own the HNIC mark and will be using the iconic brand in different ways going forward,” CBC head of public affairs Chuck Thompson told The Athletic in an email. Thompson added that the CBC would have “more to share about how (the brand will be used) in the coming weeks).”

“Hockey Night in Canada” began as a radio program in 1931 before transitioning to television on the CBC in 1952. For decades, as it aired games featuring the NHL’s biggest stars and teams, the program was the home for legendary play-by-play men including Foster Hewitt, Danny Gallivan, Dick Irvin, Bob Cole, Chris Cuthbert and Jim Hughson, and longtime show host Ron MacLean, who co-hosted the famed “Coach’s Corner” with former coach Don Cherry.

The CBC will instead air a Saturday night sports program featuring Canadian athletes competing locally and abroad, with an eye toward the upcoming 2028 Summer Olympics in Los Angeles and the 2030 Winter Olympics in the French Alps. CBC holds broadcasting rights for the Games through 2032.

“As Canada’s Olympic network every day through 2032, our increased commitment will include more in-depth storytelling, more live sport, and more coverage of Canadian athletes at home and abroad,” CBC Sports executive director Chris Wilson said, per CBC’s website. “We’re focused on the people at the heart of the competition, covering their achievements and sacrifices as they represent our country.”

In March 2025, the NHL and Rogers announced their 12-year agreement had been renewed for another 12 years. The new deal kicks in as of July 1, months ahead of the 2026-27 NHL season, and it is worth $11.2 billion Canadian. It remains to be seen if Sportsnet will sublicense games to Amazon, as it did for the last two seasons, or what agreement it might reach with a French-language broadcaster such as TVA Sports.

Regardless, even without the “Hockey Night in Canada” brand, NHL games will continue to air on Saturday nights.

“Saturday night NHL hockey is woven into the fabric of Canada and our partners at Sportsnet will continue this great tradition, as they have for the last 12 years,” NHL chief communications officer Jon Weinstein told The Athletic.
